recommendation: Keep the audit commit as an external-repo decision. If the current rendered UCUM page remains unacceptable, follow up in the FHIR publisher or tx.fhir.org terminology service so all-code UCUM expansions are refused or marked unclosed/incomplete consistently with current $expand guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-12438 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU2 FHIR-core request to stop showing a misleading finite/common UCUM expansion because UCUM is intensional.
initial_application: Jira says the issue was fixed as part of the R3 marathon. The linked 2016 Zulip trail shows the intended fix was for the spec/publisher terminology expansion to refuse full UCUM expansion or clearly direct readers to common UCUM rather than present common codes as all UCUM.
additional_context: FHIR-12464 removed the duplicate US Core UCUM value set in favor of core ucum-units. Later FHIR-36010 confirms ucum-units has no explicitly defined source expansion and that changing expansion membership is tooling or tx.fhir.org work. Current ValueSet.$expand source guidance says unbounded value sets such as UCUM should error or use valueset-unclosed when incomplete, while build.fhir.org currently shows a tx.fhir.org-generated finite expansion with no unclosed marker.
reconciliation: No source files were edited. The authoritative source/datatypes/valueset-ucum-units.xml definition is a compose-only include of http://unitsofmeasure.org with no expansion element, and no local source/config mechanism was found to suppress the generated tx.fhir.org expansion.

related_jiras.note: US Core issue removed the duplicate US Core UCUM value set and redirected users to core ucum-units, confirming the all-UCUM versus common-UCUM distinction.
Later Published issue notes that ucum-units has no explicit source expansion and expansion content changes belong to tooling or tx.fhir.org.
Later unresolved R6 migration work for UCUM value sets; it does not provide an applied current-source fix for this expansion-display issue.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive issue asking that UCUM expansion show unable-to-expand rather than common UCUM table codes because UCUM is intensional.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes the final request and the all-UCUM versus common-UCUM problem.

evidence_items.summary: The 2016 discussion records that the spec was incorrectly getting common UCUM codes but should refuse to expand UCUM because the expansion is infinite.
evidence_items.learned: This confirms the intended application target was terminology/publisher expansion behavior, not a finite source table.

evidence_items.summary: The current ucum-units ValueSet definition includes http://unitsofmeasure.org in compose and contains no expansion element.
evidence_items.learned: The checked-in build-scope source has no embedded UCUM expansion table to remove or replace.

evidence_items.summary: The current $expand guidance says unbounded value sets such as UCUM should return an error or use valueset-unclosed when the expansion is incomplete.
evidence_items.learned: Current source already contains the general rule needed for incomplete UCUM expansions.

evidence_items.summary: Later Published issue says ucum-units has no explicitly defined expansion and that changing its expansion content would be tooling or tx.fhir.org work.
evidence_items.learned: This supports treating remaining ucum-units expansion behavior as external to the checked-in ValueSet source.

evidence_items.summary: The current HTML page shows a tx.fhir.org-generated 840-concept expansion and no unclosed marker, while the current JSON ValueSet has no embedded expansion.
evidence_items.learned: The observed current mismatch is generated by external terminology/publisher behavior rather than a source expansion in this checkout.
